UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S RULE 60(a) MOTION TO CLARIFY OR CORRECT ECF NO. 108

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 60(a) for an order clarifying one passage of the Order signed and filed October 29, 2026 and entered October 30, 2026 (ECF No. 108), and correcting that passage only if an oversight, omission, or unintended ambiguity prevents it from expressing the determination the Court intended when it issued the Order. Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick signed ECF No. 108. This Motion is presented to him. Plaintiff does not request a different determination. Plaintiff requests that the written Order conform to the determination actually made on October 29, 2026. A Memorandum in Support under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) and a Proposed Order accompany this Motion.

I.	THE PASSAGE AND THE REQUESTED CORRECTION

1.	ECF No. 108 denied without prejudice Plaintiff’s Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order and, as Necessary, an Initial Pretrial Conference (ECF No. 103) and Plaintiff’s Motion for an Order Directing Completion of the Rule 26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan (ECF No. 105). ECF No. 108 at 1–2.

2.	ECF No. 108 states: “Here, the record reflects that the District Judge has chosen to refrain from beginning any discovery until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss.” ECF No. 108 at 2. The attribution immediately precedes the denial and supplies a stated premise for it.

3.	The passage identifies the District Judge as the officer who made the described choice. The passage does not identify the order, instruction, or other action on which that attribution rests.

4.	The passage describes a choice concerning “any discovery.” Page 1 of ECF No. 108 identifies four requests: entry of a scheduling order; an order directing completion of a Rule 26(f) conference and the filing of discovery plans; an initial pretrial conference; and, for any postponed step, a statement of the date or event on which scheduling will next be addressed. ECF No. 108 at 1. The Order does not state whether the attributed choice was understood to concern substantive discovery only or also the scheduling and planning steps the Order identifies.

II.	GROUNDS

5.	Plaintiff has examined the District Judge’s docketed orders and notices in this action: ECF Nos. 12, 25, 48, 50, and 70. Each addresses a subject other than the timing of discovery, the Rule 26(f) conference, or the Rule 16(b) schedule.

6.	ECF No. 84 addresses discovery timing. It states that “discovery has not officially begun in this case” and that “currently there is no Scheduling Order in this case.” ECF No. 84 at 1–2. Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis signed ECF No. 84.

7.	The documents Plaintiff reviewed do not identify the action described in ECF No. 108. Plaintiff does not treat that absence as proof that no instruction existed. Local Civil Rule 72 recognizes assignment and referral “by an order entered in the action or on the instructions of a district judge.” An instruction need not appear in a separately entered order.

8.	Rule 60(a) permits the Court to correct “a mistake arising from oversight or omission” in an order. The Fourth Circuit reads that phrase to include an inconsistency between the text of an order and the court’s intent when it entered the order, and “an unintended ambiguity that obfuscates the court’s original intent.” Sartin v. McNair Law Firm PA, 756 F.3d 259, 265–66 (4th Cir. 2014). The power is limited by the court’s original intent. Id. at 266. Plaintiff seeks correction only if the wording fails, through a qualifying oversight, omission, or unintended ambiguity, to express that intent.

9.	Plaintiff does not contend that an omitted citation establishes a correctable mistake, or that an intentional inference is a drafting error because it may be disputed. If the passage accurately expresses the original determination, Rule 60(a) requires no textual change, and Plaintiff requests none.

III.	LIMITS

10.	This Motion does not request that the Court grant ECF No. 103 or ECF No. 105, enter a scheduling order, authorize discovery, set new deadlines, make new findings justifying postponement, resolve the successor-designation question presented in ECF Nos. 97–99, or reconsider the substance of the October 29, 2026 disposition.

11.	Plaintiff’s pending submissions concerning ECF Nos. 63, 64, 65, 84, and 96 (ECF Nos. 66, 67, 76, 89, 90, 91, 93, 94, 97, 98, 99) remain pending on their own terms. No request is withdrawn by this Motion.

12.	This Motion does not extend, and does not substitute for compliance with, the period for objections to ECF No. 108 under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 72(a).

IV.	RELIEF REQUESTED

13.	Plaintiff requests a written order that:

(a)	to the extent necessary to address a qualifying omission or unintended ambiguity, clarifies whether the passage quoted in paragraph 2 describes an order or instruction of the District Judge, an inference or determination by the Magistrate Judge, or another identified judicial action, and, for an order or instruction, identifies it by date and docket citation where available or by its operative terms;

(b)	clarifies how the action so identified was understood, when ECF No. 108 issued, to relate to entry of a scheduling order, the initial pretrial conference, the parties’ Rule 26(f) conference, and the discovery-plan report, and whether ECF No. 108 was intended only to deny the requested orders without prejudice or also to recognize or direct postponement of the planning steps requested in ECF No. 105;

(c)	if, and only if, the existing text fails to express the determination actually intended on October 29, 2026, corrects the identified passage by stating the replacement language; and

(d)	leaves the denial without prejudice of ECF Nos. 103 and 105 unchanged through this Motion, creates no new scheduling, discovery, disclosure, or reporting obligation, and resolves no separately filed application.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court enter the accompanying Proposed Order.
